milestone: M12 External Mode Pack Execution Policy

strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Adds explicit Rust-owned activation of a local Mode Pack candidate into a bounded active snapshot used for mode resolution.
Existing mode.list, mode.get, permission.check, task.start, and provenance paths consume the runtime active snapshot instead of caller or VSIX policy.
Activation persists bounded metadata, fingerprints, and compiled policy summaries without raw Mode Pack JSON or raw ledger payloads.
Headless callers can rely on replay-safe active external mode policy after activation without repeated live candidate reads.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances mode_pack_runtime directly, with supporting runtime_permission_enforcement, persistent_structured_ledger, and headless_autonomous_development.
answers.new_capability: The Rust runtime can explicitly activate one validated local .brownie/modepack.json candidate into a bounded active Mode Pack snapshot.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: Existing M12/M21 behavior loads or revalidates the live Mode Pack file; it does not distinguish candidate policy from runtime-activated active policy.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: External Mode Packs remain loadable but not activatable, blocking safe remote fetch, diff, replace, and rollback lifecycle work.
answers.non_duplicative: Yes. M12.1/M12.2/M21.1 covered handoff and provenance revalidation; M12.3 adds the activation lifecycle boundary.
answers.no_new_rpc: No. A mutating activation action is required because mode.list and mode.get are read paths and must not activate as a side effect.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The result is bounded activation state and replay metadata, not a report/history/digest/readiness wrapper.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: modepack.activate validates and compiles the candidate, persists a bounded active snapshot, and mode.list/mode.get/permission.check/task.start consume that snapshot before live candidate reads.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: Headless callers can activate external mode policy once and then rely on replay-safe Rust-owned state even if the live candidate later changes.
answers.milestone_progress: M12 gains its missing explicit local Mode Pack activation boundary and can later decide if replace or rollback is required before closeout.

exit_criteria: modepack.activate requires explicit authorization and rejects missing, malformed, duplicate, unsafe, or built-in-conflicting candidates before activation
A valid local candidate writes one bounded active snapshot with compiled policy summaries, mode IDs, fingerprints, activation timestamp, and activation event id
Replaying the same activation returns the persisted activation fingerprint and does not append duplicate activation evidence
mode.list, mode.get, permission.check, and task.start consume the active snapshot after activation even when the live candidate file changes or is removed
Conflicting active snapshot replacement is denied or deferred rather than silently overwriting active policy

Ledger, RPC, store, and VSIX payloads contain no raw Mode Pack JSON, prompt, provider response, file content, stdout/stderr, command, environment, raw ledger payload, absolute path, canonical path, or secret
VSIX validators accept valid activation results and reject malformed fingerprints or raw payload fields

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M12.3 changes product runtime/protocol/store/VSIX behavior and phase manifests; review must confirm this is active snapshot execution, not another wrapper surface.
